question: During the Basic Control Skills test, what is scored as a "pull-up"?
choice_a: Stopping the vehicle without changing direction
choice_b: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
choice_c: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position
choice_d: Backing up during a forward-moving exercise
explanation: The manual states that "pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position is scored as a 'pull-up.'" Stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Basic Control Skills Test Scoring (Pull-ups)

question: Pull-ups are scored on which two exercises of the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Exercise 2 -- Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing
choice_b: Exercise 3 -- Forward Offset Tracking only
choice_c: Exercise 1 -- Forward Stop and Exercise 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing
choice_d: Exercise 1 -- Forward Stop and Exercise 3 -- Forward Offset Tracking
explanation: The manual specifies that pull-up exercises "include Exercise 2 -- Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Basic Control Skills Test Scoring (Pull-ups)

question: "Back-ups" -- backing up during a forward-moving exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position -- are scored on which exercise?
choice_b: Exercise 3 -- Forward Offset Tracking
choice_c: Exercise 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing
choice_d: Exercise 2 -- Straight-Line Backing
explanation: The manual states: "'Back-ups' will be scored on Exercise 3 -- Forward Offset Tracking."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Basic Control Skills Test Scoring (Back-ups)

question: What is defined as an "encroachment" during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Taking longer than expected to complete an exercise
choice_b: Asking the examiner a clarifying question before starting
choice_c: Sounding the horn before completing an exercise
choice_d: Crossing over or touching an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors or unique parts at door mirror height or higher
explanation: Encroachments are defined as "crossing over or touching exercise boundary lines or cones with any portion of your vehicle, other than the vehicle's mirrors (door or fender) or other unique vehicle parts at door mirror height or higher."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Basic Control Skills Test Scoring (Encroachments)

question: How many free pull-ups are you allowed on Exercise 2 -- Straight-Line Backing?
choice_b: One
choice_c: Two
choice_d: Three
explanation: The manual states, "You are allowed one (1) free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one (1) time to check around the vehicle" during Exercise 2.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Exercise 2 -- Straight Line Backing

question: How many free pull-ups are permitted during Exercise 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_b: One
choice_c: Three
choice_d: Two
explanation: The manual states, "You are allowed two (2) free pull-ups and may exit the vehicle a maximum of two (2) times to check around the vehicle during this exercise."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Exercise 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing

question: On Exercise 2 -- Straight-Line Backing, how many free "looks" (safe exits to check the vehicle's position) are you allowed?
choice_b: One
choice_c: Two
choice_d: Three
explanation: The manual states you "may be allowed a maximum of one (1) free look on Exercise 2 -- Straight-line Backing."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Basic Control Skills Test Scoring (Looks)

question: On Exercise 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing, how many free "looks" are you allowed to check the vehicle's position?
choice_b: Zero
choice_c: One
choice_d: Four
explanation: The manual states you may be allowed "two (2) free looks on Exercise 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing, to check the position of your vehicle."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Basic Control Skills Test Scoring (Looks)

question: Before safely exiting the vehicle to take a "look" during a backing exercise, what must you do?
choice_b: Set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral
choice_c: Sound the horn twice
choice_d: Ask the examiner to exit the vehicle first
explanation: The manual instructs that when exiting to check the vehicle's position, "you must set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral," then exit safely while facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Basic Control Skills Test Scoring (Looks)

question: When exiting or entering a bus (as opposed to another commercial vehicle) to check its position, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Exit through the rear emergency door only
choice_b: Face forward and maintain a firm grasp on the handrail
choice_c: Face away from the bus and use two points of contact
choice_d: There is no special procedure for buses
explanation: For buses, the manual specifies that when exiting/entering "you may face forward and maintain a firm grasp on the handrail," rather than facing the vehicle and using three points of contact as with other vehicles.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Basic Control Skills Test Scoring (Looks)

question: What happens if you open the vehicle door while the vehicle is still moving (not in neutral and parked)?
choice_a: Nothing, as long as the door is closed again quickly
choice_b: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_c: It is scored as an encroachment
choice_d: It is only counted as one "look"
explanation: The manual warns: "If you open your door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park), it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Basic Control Skills Test Scoring (Looks)

question: During Exercise 1 -- Forward Stop, how many times may you stop the vehicle?
choice_b: Only once
choice_c: As many times as needed to get it right
choice_d: Three times maximum
explanation: The manual states for Exercise 1: "Drive forward through the alley and stop with the front most part of the vehicle...within the box at the end of the alley without going past it. You may stop only once."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Exercise 1 -- Forward Stop

question: After completing Exercise 1 -- Forward Stop, what must you do before the examiner scores the exercise?
choice_b: Roll down the window and wave to the examiner
choice_c: Turn off the engine and exit the vehicle
choice_d: Set the parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound the horn
explanation: The manual instructs: "When you have stopped, set your parking brake, shift to neural and sound the horn. The examiner will then score the exercise."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Exercise 1 -- Forward Stop

question: Exercise 2 -- Straight-Line Backing requires you to back through the alley until what happens?
choice_a: The front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley
choice_b: The examiner signals with a flag
choice_c: Ten seconds have elapsed
choice_d: The rear of the vehicle clears the first set of cones
explanation: The manual instructs to "back straight through the alley until the front of your vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Exercise 2 -- Straight Line Backing

question: In Exercise 3 -- Forward Offset Tracking, which part of the vehicle must you keep between the cone and the line as you steer left through the opening?
choice_b: The left mirror
choice_c: The right most rear tire
choice_d: The rear bumper
explanation: The manual states you must drive forward and steer left "keeping the right most rear tire between the cone and the line."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Exercise 3 -- Forward Offset Tracking

question: How many free back-ups are allowed on Exercise 3 -- Forward Offset Tracking, and may you exit the vehicle during this exercise?
choice_a: One free back-up is allowed, and you may exit once
choice_b: There are no free back-ups, and you are not permitted to exit the vehicle
choice_c: Unlimited back-ups are allowed, but exiting is prohibited
choice_d: Two free back-ups are allowed, and exiting is unrestricted
explanation: The manual states plainly: "There are NO free back-ups, and you are NOT permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Exercise 3 -- Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing, the rear most part of the vehicle must be brought to within how many feet of the rear of the alley?
choice_b: Ten feet
choice_c: One foot
choice_d: Five feet
explanation: The manual states you must bring "the rear most part of your vehicle...within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley," stopping in the three-foot box at the end of the alley.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Exercise 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing

question: In the standard order of the Basic Control Skills test, which step is the Reverse Offset Backing exercise?
choice_b: Step 1
choice_c: Step 2
choice_d: Step 3
explanation: The manual lists the sequence as "Step 1 -- Forward Stop, Step 2 -- Straight-Line Backing, Step 3 -- Forward Offset Tracking, and Step 4 -- Reverse Offset Backing."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Basic Control Skills Test Exercises

question: According to the manual, what must happen before an applicant may proceed to the Road Test?
choice_a: The applicant must complete a 24-hour waiting period
choice_b: The applicant must first pass the Basic Control Skills test
choice_c: There is no prerequisite; both tests can be taken in any order
choice_d: The applicant must retake the written knowledge test
explanation: The manual states directly: "Remember, the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before you can proceed to the Road Test."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Road Test

question: What may result from failing to follow the examiner's instructions or committing an unsafe act during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: A mandatory retake scheduled for the following week
choice_b: Automatic failure and possible termination of the test by the examiner
choice_c: A verbal warning only, with no effect on scoring
choice_d: A single point deduction
explanation: The manual states that failure to follow instructions or committing an unsafe act "may result in an automatic failure and the test may be terminated by the examiner."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 13, Failure to Follow Instructions or Unsafe Act

question: If your on-road test route does not include a particular traffic situation, such as a railroad crossing, what may the examiner ask you to do?
choice_a: Reschedule the test for a route that includes it
choice_b: Skip that portion of the scoring entirely
choice_c: Simulate the traffic situation by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing
choice_d: Automatically receive full points for that maneuver
explanation: The manual explains: "If your test route does not have certain traffic situations, you may be asked to simulate a traffic situation. You will do this by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, How You Will Be Tested

question: According to the manual, what defines "unsafe coasting" while approaching a turn?
choice_a: Coasting for more than 10 seconds regardless of distance
choice_b: Coasting through any intersection
choice_c: The vehicle being out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
choice_d: Coasting downhill at any speed
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring "when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, How You Will Be Tested -- Turns

question: When completing a turn on the on-road test, where should the vehicle finish?
choice_b: In the correct lane, without moving into oncoming traffic
choice_c: In the left-most lane regardless of turn direction
choice_d: Straddling two lanes briefly before merging
explanation: The manual states that when turning, the "vehicle should not move into oncoming traffic" and "should finish turn in correct lane."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, How You Will Be Tested -- Turns

question: If you must stop behind another vehicle before an intersection or turn, what is the recommended way to judge a safe gap?
choice_a: Stop as close as possible without touching bumpers
choice_b: Stop where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
choice_c: Stop exactly one car length behind
choice_d: Stop close enough to see the vehicle's rear license plate clearly
explanation: The manual instructs: "If stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you (safe gap)."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, How You Will Be Tested -- Turns/Intersections

question: According to the manual, what should you avoid doing while proceeding through an intersection?
choice_b: Keeping your hands on the wheel
choice_c: Decelerating and yielding to pedestrians
choice_d: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
explanation: The manual instructs that when driving through an intersection, you should "not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, How You Will Be Tested -- Intersections

question: During the Urban/Rural Straight portion of the on-road test, where should your vehicle be positioned and how should its speed relate to the flow of traffic?
choice_a: Centered in the right-most lane, keeping up with traffic flow but not exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_b: Centered in the left-most lane, exceeding traffic flow when safe
choice_c: Straddling the center line, matching the fastest vehicle
choice_d: Anywhere in the roadway, at a fixed 5 mph under the limit
explanation: The manual states the vehicle "should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane), and you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, How You Will Be Tested -- Urban/Rural Straight

question: During the multiple-lane portion of the on-road test, what lane change sequence will you typically be asked to perform?
choice_a: Change lanes three separate times in the same direction
choice_b: Remain in the same lane throughout
choice_c: Change lanes to the left, then back to the right
choice_d: Change lanes to the right only
explanation: The manual states: "During multiple lane portions of the test, you will be asked to change lanes to the left and then back to the right."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, How You Will Be Tested -- Lane Changes

question: According to the manual, what must all commercial drivers avoid doing while any part of the vehicle is in a railroad crossing?
choice_b: Braking smoothly before the crossing
choice_c: Stopping, changing gears, passing another vehicle, or changing lanes
choice_d: Keeping their hands on the steering wheel
explanation: The manual states: "Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in the crossing."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, How You Will Be Tested -- Railroad Crossing

question: If you are driving a bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards, at what distance from the nearest rail must you stop before a non-exempt railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet
choice_b: Exactly 10 feet from the nearest rail
choice_c: Within 20 feet but not less than 5 feet
choice_d: Within 100 feet but not less than 25 feet
explanation: The manual states these drivers should "stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail, place the bus in park/neutral and set the parking brake."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, How You Will Be Tested -- Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the on-road test, what might the examiner ask you to report?
choice_a: The speed limit on the overpass
choice_b: The posted clearance or height
choice_c: The name of the road above
choice_d: The posted weight limit
explanation: The manual states: "After driving under an overpass, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, How You Will Be Tested -- Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: After driving over a bridge during the on-road test, what might the examiner ask you to identify?
choice_b: The number of lanes on the bridge
choice_c: The posted weight limit
choice_d: The posted clearance
explanation: The manual states: "After going over a bridge, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted weight limit was."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, How You Will Be Tested -- Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: For a manual transmission vehicle, what does the manual say about clutch usage during the on-road test?
choice_b: Ride the clutch to control speed on hills
choice_c: Always use the clutch to shift and double-clutch when shifting, without revving or lugging the engine
choice_d: Coast with the clutch depressed whenever convenient
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to "always use clutch to shift," "double-clutch when shifting," and not to "rev or lug the engine," while explicitly warning against riding the clutch, coasting with it depressed, or popping it.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, General Driving Behaviors -- Clutch Usage

question: According to the manual's Gear Usage guidance, when should a driver avoid shifting gears?
choice_b: On straight rural roads
choice_c: While in turns and intersections
choice_d: On expressway entrance ramps
explanation: The manual's Gear Usage section states: "Do not shift in turns and intersections."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, General Driving Behaviors -- Gear Usage

question: On a multiple-lane road, where should a driver finish a left turn according to the manual's Lane Usage guidance?
choice_a: In the lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_b: In the left-most lane
choice_c: In any lane that is open
choice_d: In the curb lane
explanation: The manual specifies drivers should "complete a turn in the proper lane on a multiple lane road (vehicle should finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line)."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, General Driving Behaviors -- Lane Usage

question: When braking on a downgrade using the "snubbing" technique, at what point should the brakes be released after applying them?
choice_a: When speed has been reduced to 10 mph below the "safe" speed
choice_b: Immediately after applying them, regardless of speed change
choice_c: When speed has been reduced to 5 mph below the "safe" speed
choice_d: Only once the vehicle has come to a complete stop
explanation: The manual states: "When speed has been reduced to 5 mph below the 'safe' speed, release the brakes," and gives the example of a 40 mph safe speed being reduced to 35 mph before releasing.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, General Driving Behaviors -- Upgrade and Downgrade

question: What is the braking technique described in the manual, in which brakes are applied hard enough to feel a definite slowdown and then released at a set speed, called?
choice_b: Snubbing
choice_c: Riding
choice_d: Pumping
explanation: The manual states: "This braking technique is called 'snubbing.'"
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, General Driving Behaviors -- Upgrade and Downgrade

question: As of what effective date does Illinois law prohibit the use of hand-held cellphones, texting, or other communication devices while operating a motor vehicle?
explanation: The manual states: "Effective Jan. 1, 2014, Illinois law prohibits the use of hand-held cellphones, texting or using other communication devices while operating a motor vehicle."
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, Electronic Device Law

question: Which of the following is listed as a recognized exemption allowing Illinois drivers to use a cellphone or text message while driving?
choice_a: Checking directions on a map app while moving
choice_b: Any use as long as speed is under 25 mph
choice_c: Reporting an emergency situation
choice_d: Texting a passenger seated in the vehicle
explanation: The manual lists exemptions including "Reporting an emergency situation," using the device hands-free or voice-activated, being parked on the shoulder, or being stopped due to obstructed traffic with the vehicle in neutral or park.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, Electronic Device Law

question: According to the manual, who is permitted to use a hands-free device or Bluetooth technology while driving?
choice_b: Only commercial drivers with a hazmat endorsement
choice_c: No one -- hands-free devices are fully banned
choice_d: Persons over age 18
explanation: The manual states: "Hands-free devices or Blue Tooth technology is allowed for persons over age 18," though it notes this is still considered a distraction.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, Electronic Device Law

question: If you are applying for a School Bus endorsement, what will the on-road test require you to demonstrate?
choice_b: Backing into a loading dock
choice_c: Coupling and uncoupling a trailer
choice_d: Parallel parking on a hill
explanation: The manual states: "If you are applying for a School Bus endorsement, you will be required to demonstrate loading and unloading students," referring the reader to Section 10 for the procedures.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 14, How You Will Be Tested -- Student Discharge (School Bus)
